detail.longDescription: The code below contains a asynchronous def that sends a request to a OAuth2 server endpoint and when the server returns 200 , the client is redirected to the given redirect point called redirect_uri which is inside of params and inserts two parameters at the url which are code and state ( state is optional based off the API's official documents). async def get_access_token(self, refreshing): async with self.session.get("oauth2 api endpoint", params={ "response_type": "code", "client_id": self.client_id, "redirect_uri": "https://example.com" # << Redirected automatically to this when the response is 200. }, headers={ "Content-Type": "application/json", "User-Agents": "api/v0.0.1a" }) as response: self.__log(response.url, "info") if response.status == 200: self.access_token = response.url.query.get("code") # << Get code paramater here return self.access_token else: self.__log(f"Server returned {response.status} and {response.json if not response.text else response.text}.", "err") The main issue here is that the response.url doesn't change to redirect_uri to retrieve the parameters using url.query.get on the code but it's root API page. Example: GET >> "https://api.web/login" >> if 200 >> "https://redirecting.url/?code=placeholder&state=placeholder" >> but instead >> "https://api.web/onboarding" == the value for response.url (Disclaimer: this code belongs into a class , which explains why there's self and a private function being called in this function and it can be ignored)
